events.title: The excommunication of Martin Luther
events.shortBlurb: By the bull Decet Romanum Pontificem, Pope Leo X formally excommunicated Martin Luther, sealing the breach of the Reformation…
body: On 3 January 1521 Pope Leo X issued the bull Decet Romanum Pontificem, which pronounced the formal excommunication of Martin Luther, an Augustinian friar and professor of Scripture at Wittenberg who had refused every summons to retract, and cut him off from the communion of the Church.

The sentence carried out the threat of the bull Exsurge Domine of 15 June 1520, which had condemned forty-one propositions drawn from Luther's writings and given him sixty days to recant. Luther had answered on 10 December 1520 by burning the bull, with volumes of canon law, before the Elster Gate of Wittenberg.

The sentence did not end the movement but hardened it. The following April Luther stood before the emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms and refused again to retract, and in May the Edict of Worms laid him under the ban of the empire. The definitive rupture of Western Christendom was underway.
